Every other watchdog/editor contract test in that CI step already runs in both release gates.
  Why it fails at runtime: A future change that breaks the guarded reap idiom could land on the default branch via a path that bypasses CI (e.g. a direct push or a merge-conflict resolution commit from a workflow) and then pass both release gates undetected. The release would tag `@stable` with a broken watchdog reap, and on the `orchestrator/project-3965` branch (where `sudo -u nobody` isolation makes the already-exited-watchdog race deterministic), every wall-time/idle editor kill would abort the entire review run instead of costing one attempt. The sibling test `test_review_editor_fifo_drain.py` is in both release gates, so its absence for this test is not a policy choice — it is a gap.
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=5

A regression in the guarded-reap idiom could pass CI on a PR (if the PR author forgets to update the test) and ship in a @stable release undetected by the release gates.
